spec: Fix round 1 for T-1216: review T-1227 requested changes. fix round 1: address review T-1227 comment orchestrator/worker_control.py:236 [med]: steer() sets the registry to 'steering' and bumps the epoch before delivery. If steer_resume or resume_worker raises (for example the claude binary is missing, or the codex thread is locked), nothing restores the status or records a failure. The task stays in 'steering', and daemon.reconcile_dead now skips 'steering' entries, so nothing ever recovers it. Wrap delivery in try/except: on failure, re fix round 1: address review T-1227 comment orchestrator/worker_control.py:209 [med]: When the recorded pid is None (a claude worker still launching, or a worker whose pid was not yet registered), _terminate is a no-op but steer() still resumes the same session or thread. That gives two concurrent writers on one worktree and one session or thread. The pid guard rejects only unsafe pids, not a missing one. Refuse when pid is None or not alive, or wait until it is. fix round 1: address review T-1227 comment orchestrator/worker_control.py:240 [low]: The 'steered' event that returns the status to running is written only after the resume call returns. If resume_worker or steer_resume blocks until the resumed run finishes, the registry shows 'steering' for the whole run, and the guard skips 'steered' because the entry is already terminal. Confirm the resume launch sets 'running' itself; otherwise write 'steered' from the launch path. fix round 1 rule: steer(): wrap delivery (steer_resume / resume_worker) in try/except; on failure record a terminal failed state on the registry with the reason, release the pool reservation through release_if_current, restore the bus task to its previous status with a steer_failed note, and re-raise. Refuse (no interrupt, no epoch bump) when the registry pid is None or not alive, with a clear error. The resume launch path itself writes the steered event and sets status running before the resumed run starts, so a blocking resume never leaves the entry in steering. Add tests for delivery failure recovery and for the pid-None refusal. Run .claude/hooks/tests-green.sh . until it exits 0; do not ask questions; report files changed and failures-only output.

If resume_worker or steer_resume blocks until the resumed run finishes, the registry shows 'steering' for the whole run, and the guard skips 'steered' because the entry is already terminal. fix round 1 rule: steer(): wrap delivery (steer_resume / resume_worker) in try/except; on failure record a terminal failed state on the registry with the reason, release the pool reservation through release_if_current, restore the bus task to its previous status with a steer_failed note, and re-raise. Refuse (no interrupt, no epoch bump) when the registry pid is None or not alive, with a clear error. The resume launch path itself writes the steered event and sets status running before the resumed run starts, so a blocking resume never leaves the entry in steering. Add tests for delivery failure recovery and for the pid-None refusal.

result.summary: All three fix-round findings are addressed. steer() now refuses when the pid is None or not alive, before any record or epoch bump. Delivery is wrapped in try/except: on failure it marks the registry failed, records steer_failed, restores the bus status and releases the pool reservation via release_if_current, then re-raises. The 'steered'/running event is written by the resume launch paths before communicate() (executor.py:177-179, spawn.py:1193-1194), so a blocking resume no longer leaves the entry in 'steering'. The commit adds tests for delivery-failure recovery, missing or dead pid refusal, and preserving a newer epoch. I did not run the test suite.

comments.issue: On delivery failure the bus task is restored to its previous status (usually 'running') with pid=None, while the registry entry is 'failed'. This follows the spec, but nothing else in the scoped diff confirms the daemon's reconcile path will requeue a task that is 'running' with no pid.

The pid liveness check runs under the bus lock, but the _terminate call that follows runs after the lock is released. A pid reused between the two would be signalled. This is a narrow race, and the pid <= 1 and own-pid guards remain.
